fullPassage: When you are about to go on stage or perhaps take the microphone in a work presentation, do you feel sweaty, get flushed, have a dry mouth, or taste metal? Before taking an exam, does your breathing quicken? These are signs of your body activating your stress response or sympathetic nervous system. But stress is bad, right? Actually, stress isn't always bad. In fact, there are two types of stress: distress (what we normally think of as "stress") and eustress (beneficial stress that motivates us). Coming from the same root as the word euphoria ("eu" meaning good), eustress has been shown to induce different physiological changes to distress, including less strain on your cardiovascular system and a burst of the love hormone oxytocin, which helps heal damage to your heart. Meditation techniques can channel distress into eustress to help you approach whatever challenge or task you face with a clear, calm mind that is ready to focus.

det.korean: ② having → have. or로 연결된 병렬 구조: feel, get, have, taste — 모두 원형이어야 한다.
det.analysis: Do you feel / get / have / taste? 형태로 do의 병렬 구조이므로 have가 맞다.
det.tip: 병렬 구조에서 모든 동사는 같은 형태(원형)로 통일되어야 한다.

questions.stem:

det.analysis: 관계대명사절 'that motivates us'에서 that의 선행사는 단수 eustress이므로 motivates(3단현)가 올바르다.
det.tip: 관계대명사절의 동사는 선행사의 수에 일치시켜야 한다.

questions.stem:

det.korean: ④ what → which. 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법 관계대명사는 which이다.
det.analysis: 콤마+which는 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법이다. what은 선행사를 내포하는 관계대명사이므로 이 자리에 불가.
det.tip: 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 관계대명사는 반드시 which이다.

det.analysis: 'ready to + 동사원형' 구문에서 to부정사 to focus가 필요하다. focusing(현재분사/동명사)은 불가.

questions.passage: When you are about to go on stage or perhaps take the microphone in a work presentation, do you feel sweaty, get flushed, have a dry mouth, or taste metal? Before taking an exam, does your breathing quicken? These are signs of your body activating your stress response or sympathetic nervous system. But stress is bad, right? Actually, stress isn't always bad. In fact, there are two types of stress: distress (what we normally think of as "stress") and eustress (beneficial stress that motivates us). Coming from the same root as the word euphoria ("eu" meaning good), eustress has been shown to induce different physiological changes to distress, including less strain on your cardiovascular system and a burst of the love hormone oxytocin, which helps heal damage to your heart. Meditation techniques can channel distress into eustress to help you approach whatever challenge or task you face with a clear, calm mind that is ready to focus.

det.korean: 본문의 'the love hormone oxytocin'에서 oxytocin을 찾는 문제.
det.analysis: oxytocin은 eustress가 유발하는 긍정적 생리 변화 중 하나로, 심장 치유에도 도움을 준다.
det.tip: oxytocin = love hormone, 심장 치유 역할.
